title: Spiral Visualisation for Time Series
code: library(tsspiral) library(ggplot2) library(viridis) #> Loading required package: viridisLite  monthly_data <- data.frame(   date = seq.Date(     as.Date("2020-01-01"),     as.Date("2024-12-01"),     by = "month"   ) )  monthly_data$value <- rnorm(   nrow(monthly_data),   mean = 100,   sd = 20 )  ggplot(   monthly_data,   aes(     x = date,     y = value,     fill = value   ) ) +   geom_tsspiral(     ring_spacing = 2   ) +   scale_fill_viridis_c() +   theme_void() ggplot(   monthly_data,   aes(     x = date,     y = value,     fill = value   ) ) +   geom_tsspiral(     ring_spacing = 1   ) +   scale_fill_viridis_c() +   theme_void() monthly_data <- data.frame(   date = seq.Date(     as.Date("2020-02-01"),     as.Date("2024-12-01"),     by = "month"   ) )  monthly_data$value <- rnorm(   nrow(monthly_data),   mean = 100,   sd = 20 )  ggplot(   monthly_data,   aes(     x = date,     y = value,     fill = value   ) ) +   geom_tsspiral(     ring_spacing = 2   ) +   scale_fill_viridis_c() +   theme_void()

title: Spiral Visualisation for Time Series
code: set.seed(123)  dat <- data.frame(   date = seq.Date(    as.Date("2020-01-01"),    as.Date("2023-12-31"),     by = "day"    )  )  dat$value <- 100 +  20 * sin(     2 * pi *        lubridate::yday(dat$date) / 365    ) +   rnorm(      nrow(dat),      sd = 5    )   ggplot(   dat,   aes(     x = date,     y = value,    fill = value   ) ) +   geom_tsspiral(     ring_spacing = 2    ) +    scale_fill_viridis_c() +    theme_void()

title: Spiral Visualisation for Time Series
code: set.seed(123)  dat <- data.frame(   date = seq.Date(     as.Date("2020-01-01"),     as.Date("2023-12-31"),     by = "day"   ) )  doy <- lubridate::yday(dat$date)  dat$value <-   20 +   15 * sin(2 * pi * doy / 365) +   35 * exp(-((doy - 100) / 20)^2) +   25 * exp(-((doy - 280) / 30)^2) +   rnorm(nrow(dat), 0, 3)  ggplot(   dat,   aes(     x = date,     y = value,     fill = value   ) ) +   geom_tsspiralbar(     ring_spacing = 2   ) +   scale_fill_viridis_c() +   theme_void() library(ggplot2)  set.seed(123)  dat <- data.frame(   date = seq.Date(     as.Date("2020-01-01"),     as.Date("2023-12-31"),     by = "day"   ) )  dat$value <- 100 +   30 * sin(     2 * pi * lubridate::yday(dat$date) / 365   ) +   rnorm(     nrow(dat),     sd = 8   )  ggplot(   dat,   aes(     x = date,     y = value,     fill = value   ) ) +   geom_tsspiralbar(     ring_spacing = 2   ) +   scale_fill_viridis_c() +   theme_void()

title: Spiral Visualisation for Time Series
code: library(ggplot2)  set.seed(123)  # Generate a daily time series spiral_dat <- data.frame(   date = seq.Date(     from = as.Date("2020-01-01"),     to = as.Date("2023-12-31"),     by = "day"   ) )  # Generate a seasonal time series spiral_dat$value <-   100 +   25 * sin(     2 * pi * lubridate::yday(spiral_dat$date) / 365   ) +   rnorm(     nrow(spiral_dat),     sd = 5   )  # Create missing periods missing_dates <- c(   seq.Date(     as.Date("2020-03-01"),     as.Date("2020-03-20"),     by = "day"   ),   seq.Date(     as.Date("2021-07-10"),     as.Date("2021-08-05"),     by = "day"   ),   seq.Date(     as.Date("2023-01-15"),     as.Date("2023-02-10"),     by = "day"   ) )  # Remove missing observations spiral_dat <- spiral_dat[   !spiral_dat$date %in% missing_dates, ]  # Plot missingness ggplot(   spiral_dat,   aes(x = date) ) +   geom_tsspiralmiss(     ring_spacing = 2,     observed_colour = "grey85",     missing_colour = "black"   ) +   theme_void()

what: Calendar plot for hourly time series
title: Spiral Visualisation for Time Series
code: # ========================================================= # Example: Two months of hourly data # =========================================================  set.seed(123)  hourly_data <- tibble::tibble(   datetime = seq(     from = as.POSIXct("2026-01-01 00:00"),     to   = as.POSIXct("2026-02-28 23:00"),     by   = "hour"   ) ) |>   dplyr::mutate(     hour = lubridate::hour(datetime),     day = lubridate::day(datetime),      temperature =       25 +       4 * sin(2 * pi * hour / 24) +       0.05 * day +       stats::rnorm(         length(datetime),         0,         0.8       )   ) # January calendar_hourly_polar(   hourly_data,   datetime,   temperature,   month = "2026-01-01" ) # February calendar_hourly_polar(   hourly_data,   datetime,   temperature,   month = "2026-02-01" )

title: Spiral Visualisation for Time Series
code: set.seed(123)  dat <- data.frame(   date = seq.Date(     from = as.Date("2020-01-01"),     to = as.Date("2023-12-31"),     by = "day" ))  dat$value <- 20 +   5 * sin(     2 * pi * lubridate::yday(dat$date) / 365.25   ) +    rnorm(nrow(dat), 0, 1)  temporal_hierarchical(  data = dat,  date = date,  value = value)

what: Calendar of Hourly Polar Bar Charts — calendar_hourly_polar
title: Calendar of Hourly Polar Bar Charts — calendar_hourly_polar
text: Creates monthly calendar visualization calendar day contains 24-hour polar bar chart. bar represents one hour day, angular position corresponding hour bar length colour representing observed value.

title: Calendar of Hourly Polar Bar Charts — calendar_hourly_polar
code: calendar_hourly_polar(   data,   datetime,   value,   month = NULL,   radius = 0.35,   bar_width = 0.85,   cell_width = 1,   cell_height = 1 )

title: Calendar of Hourly Polar Bar Charts — calendar_hourly_polar
text: data data frame containing hourly observations. datetime date-time column containing observation times. value numeric column containing values visualized. month date character value specifying month plot. example, "2026-01-01". NULL, month containing earliest observation used. radius Numeric. Maximum radius hourly bars within calendar cell. Defaults 0.35. bar_width Numeric 0 1. Controls angular width hourly bar relative 24-hour sector. Defaults 0.85. cell_width Numeric. Width calendar cell. Defaults 1. cell_height Numeric. Height calendar cell. Defaults 1.

title: Calendar of Hourly Polar Bar Charts — calendar_hourly_polar
text: ggplot object containing calendar hourly polar bar charts.

title: Calendar of Hourly Polar Bar Charts — calendar_hourly_polar
text: Missing hourly observations retained calendar drawn bars. calendar arranged Monday Sunday, day positioned according calendar date. day represented separate polar bar chart containing 24 bars. Hour 0 starts top circle hours proceed clockwise hour 23. bar length scaled according range observed values selected month, colour represents original value. Missing hourly observations left blank. function useful examining intraday patterns retaining context calendar. example, daily temperature, air quality, electricity demand, traffic, regularly recorded hourly measurements can displayed.

title: Calendar of Hourly Polar Bar Charts — calendar_hourly_polar
code: set.seed(123)  hourly_data <- tibble::tibble(   datetime = seq(     from = as.POSIXct("2026-01-01 00:00"),     to = as.POSIXct("2026-01-31 23:00"),     by = "hour"   ) ) |>   dplyr::mutate(     hour = lubridate::hour(datetime),     day = lubridate::day(datetime),     temperature =       25 +       4 * sin(2 * pi * hour / 24) +       0.05 * day +       stats::rnorm(length(datetime), 0, 0.8)   )  calendar_hourly_polar(   hourly_data,   datetime,   temperature,   month = "2026-01-01" )

title: Spiral Time-Series Geometry — geom_tsspiral
text: geom_tsspiral() displays year time series radial ring. angular position represents day year. spiral always contains 365 angular divisions. spiral starts 12 o'clock January 1 proceeds clockwise year. input frequency detected automatically. Daily observations used directly. Weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual observations expanded daily observations plotting. Calendar labels displayed around outermost ring: daily data: month names, monthly data: month names, quarterly data: quarter names, weekly data: week numbers, annual data: month names. spiral uses fixed 365-day calendar. January 1 starts 12 o'clock calendar proceeds clockwise. day d, angular position $$ \theta_d = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{2\pi(d-1)}{365}. $$ Consequently, January 1 positioned 12 o'clock later days move clockwise around spiral. Leap years create 366th angular division. February 29 mapped February 28 position days February 29 shifted one day. Monthly, quarterly, weekly, annual observations expanded corresponding daily intervals. Consequently, monthly observation fills complete angular region corresponding month rather appearing thin radial slice.
